title: Material Synthesis Metadata Schema
description: A schema describing metadata fields commonly used in material synthesis research.

Linkage.description: The type of chemical bond connecting the building blocks (e.g., Boroxine, Imine, β-Ketoenamine).

Organic Ligands.description: The organic molecules that coordinate to metal ions or form the framework's backbone (e.g., Carboxylates, Imidazolates, Phosphonates).

Solvents.description: The solvents used in the synthesis reaction (e.g., Mesitylene, Dioxane, DMF).

Acids/Bases.description: Any acids or bases used as catalysts or to control crystallization.

Reaction Vessels.description: The type of container used for the reaction (e.g., Pyrex tube, autoclave).

Reaction Type.description: The general category of the chemical reaction used for synthesis.

Chiral Monomer.description: Monomers that are inherently chiral and used as building blocks.

Chiral Inducer.description: A substance that induces chirality in the final product without being incorporated into the structure.

Chiral Group.description: A functional group that imparts chirality to a molecule.

Chiral Crosslinking Agent.description: A chiral molecule used to link polymer chains.

Polymer Matrix.description: A polymer material in which the synthesized material is embedded (e.g., PVA, Polyurethane).

Photoactive Monomer.description: Monomers that are responsive to light (e.g., Porphyrins, Pyrene, Thiophene).

Heteroatomic Monomer.description: Monomers containing atoms other than carbon and hydrogen (e.g., S, N, Se, O).

Heavy Atom Group.description: Functional groups containing heavy atoms like Iodine or Bromine.

Electron Donor/ Acceptor.description: Molecules or functional groups that can donate or accept electrons.

Structural Control.description: Methods or strategies used to control the material's structure.

Defect Engineering.description: The intentional creation of defects in the material's structure.

Nano Structure.description: The nanoscale structure or morphology of the material.

Hybridization.description: The process of combining the material with other substances to form a hybrid material.

X ray absorption.description: Properties related to the material's ability to absorb X-rays.

Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence.description: Information related to the material exhibiting TADF properties.
